title: Titl · Subtitles for almost any YouTube video
metaDesc: Subtitles for almost any YouTube video, even ones with no captions at all. Transcribed on your own computer with whisper.cpp and shown on time. Free and open source.
heroLead: Even videos with no captions at all. Titl transcribes the speech on your own computer with whisper.cpp, a few seconds ahead, so each line appears with the words. Private, free and open source, in about 100 languages.
heroBrowsers: Chrome, Edge and Brave on macOS, Windows and Linux.
shotAlt: Titl showing Serbian subtitles with an English translation on a TEDx talk
shotCaption: Titl's own output on Tatjana Vojtehovski at TEDxZemun: Serbian on top, English translation below.
whyText: Most live-caption tools show each line after it's spoken, upload your audio to the cloud, or only work when YouTube already has captions. Titl runs whisper.cpp on your GPU, prepares subtitles ahead of what you're watching, and works on any video, even ones with no captions at all.
f1a: Lookahead mode: a muted copy of the video plays a few seconds ahead in a collapsed tab, so each line appears with the speech.
f1b: Live mode for live streams: subtitles 3–5 s late.
f1c: Follows seeks, speed changes, ads and video changes.
f2a: Audio only goes to 127.0.0.1, never to the cloud.
f3a: On-device translation with Chrome's built-in translator into ~36 languages.
f3b: Original and translation together, or just the translation.
f3c: Blur the translation to practise listening: V or a click reveals it.
f4a: large-v3-turbo on Metal or CUDA, small on CPU.
f4c: Serbian: always Latin or always Cyrillic, never a mix.
f5a: One helper, titl, finds or downloads whisper.cpp and a model.
f5b: Starts the server on a random free port when you press Start.
f5c: Windows: one PowerShell line, then updates from the popup.
f6a: Subtitles in normal and fullscreen, never over YouTube's controls.
f6b: Settings apply to running subtitles as soon as you save.
s1Text: Add Titl to Chrome. It also works in Edge and Brave.
s2Text: It runs whisper.cpp on your computer and downloads a model.
winRun: Double-click it. It downloads whisper.cpp and a model, sets everything up and stays open until you press Enter. If SmartScreen warns about an unknown publisher (the file isn't code-signed), open the details and choose to run it anyway.

installNote: A GPU is recommended (Apple Silicon or NVIDIA). The Whisper model takes 0.5–1.6 GB of disk. Full install guide
q1: Does my audio leave my computer?
a1: No. Titl sends audio only to the whisper.cpp server on 127.0.0.1 or localhost and refuses any other address. Translation runs on your device too. See the privacy policy.
q2: Why does a muted tab open?
a2: In lookahead mode, a muted copy of the video plays a few seconds ahead so subtitles are ready before you hear the words. It's tucked into a collapsed grey Titl tab group and closes when you stop.
a3: About 100 spoken languages, anything Whisper recognises. Translation goes into ~36 languages with Chrome's built-in translator (Chrome 138+).
a6: Turn it on in Options → Translate to. Each line is translated on your device by Chrome's built-in translator (Chrome 138+). The language pack downloads once, and no text is sent to a translation service. In lookahead mode lines are translated seconds before they appear, so there's no delay. You can show the original above the translation, or blur the translation and reveal it with V.
q4: Does it work without a GPU?
a4: Yes. On CPU the helper picks the smaller small model, which keeps up with the video. Lookahead mode gives transcription a head start, so slower machines just pause a little longer before playing.
a5: Nothing. Titl is free and MIT-licensed. If it helps you, support Titl on GitHub and/or on Ko-fi.
